newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fall, consolidate on freeze news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fall, consolidate on freeze news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased in nervous trading on rumours about another freezing of bonds but found support later when the market learnt the sum in question was not large, dealers said.

A senior official at Vneshtorgbank, the main depositary for the bonds, said on Thursday Moscow police had frozen MinFin bonds with a face value of about $180,000 this month. The total nominal value of all MinFin bonds outstanding is $11 billion.
Dealers said selling had started before the news as the market got nervous over the rumours, with volumes of frozen paper said to be as much as tens of million dollars.
"Prices found good support after the news as everybody calmed down," a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell dealer said in Moscow.
"The market got very nervous because of the rumours. If the sum had been much higher, everything would have been much worse."
Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said: "People were selling on the rumours as different figures (of frozen MinFins) but some buying started after the news."
Dealers said the most actively traded third, fourth, fifth and sixth tranches are currently supported at 87.00, 62.00-62.25, 44.00 and 50.00 respectively.
